          Reporter: thomas.friedrichsmeier at kdemail.net

Graphics text misalignment with some symbols.

Try the following code example with RK() and grDevices::X11() devices:
  plot(1, 1, sub="☀️ ☀️\nx x\n௵ ௵")

For the RK()-device the first pair of symbols is off-center, somehow.

First found in rkward 0.8.2, but probably the issue has been around for much
longer.

messages.subject: A few updated and a few new RKWard plug-ins JAN-2026
messages.subject_clean: A few updated and a few new RKWard plug-ins JAN-2026
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
Just to let you know, here is a comparison of the mirror versions with the
updated versions. I have also added a few new RKWard repositories.

n name url_mirror version_mirror url_gh version_gh comparison_mirror_gh
description
1 rk.aiken.v
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.aiken.v/index.html
0.02.8 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.aiken_v 0.02.8 TRUE An RKWard plugin
to calculate Aiken's coefficients for content validity (V) and homogeneity
(H).
2 rk.apyramid NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.apyramid 0.1.0 FALSE
Provides a graphical interface for the {apyramid} package within RKWard. It
allows users to create publication-quality population pyramids from both
standard data frames and complex survey design objects (svydesign) with
minimal effort.
3 rk.bayesian NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.bayesian 0.0.1 FALSE
It is an external plug-in for RKWard that introduces a full suite of
Bayesian statistical tests powered by the `BayesFactor` package. It is
designed to provide "Jamovi-like" output, including Bayes Factors,
posterior effect size estimates, descriptive statistics, and visualization
plots.
4 rk.cartographr NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.cartographr 0.1.2 FALSE
An RKWard plugin package for creating beautiful maps using the cartographr
R package. This plugin provides a graphical user interface (GUI) to fetch
data from OpenStreetMap and generate customizable map plots directly within
RKWard.
5 rk.class.lists NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.class.lists 0.0.1 FALSE
This package provides a suite of RKWard plugins designed to simplify the
manipulation of R object classes and data structures. It offers a graphical
interface for coercing objects (e.g., converting a matrix to a data frame),
changing vector types (e.g., numeric to factor), and performing complex
list operations (creating, appending, and extracting elements).
6 rk.codebook NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.codebook 0.0.1 FALSE
rk.codebook generates professional HTML data dictionaries directly within
RKWard. It bridges the gap between RKWard's internal variable labels and
standard R reporting tools (powered by sjPlot), allowing you to create
instant "Codebooks" for your datasets.
7 rk.cSplit
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.cSplit/index.html
0.01.9 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.cSplit 0.01.10 FALSE
An RKWard plugin to split concatenated columns into a long or wide format
using the cSplit() function from the 'splitstackshape' package.
8 rk.ctables NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.ctables 0.0.1 FALSE
rk.ctables is an RKWard plugin that brings the power of SPSS-style "Custom
Tables" (CTABLES) to R. Powered by the [expss](
https://gdemin.github.io/expss/) package, it allows you to build complex
hierarchical tables using a simple drag-and-drop interface, bridging the
gap for users migrating from SPSS to R
9 rk.data.wrangling NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.data.wrangling 0.1.2
FALSE
rk.data.wrangling brings modern, "tidy" data manipulation tools to the
RKWard GUI. It provides a user-friendly interface for the powerful dplyr
package, allowing users to perform complex batch
operations—transformations, recoding, and scoring—on multiple variables
simultaneously without writing complex code.
10 rk.dates NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.dates 0.0.2 FALSE
This package provides a single, powerful RKWard plugin designed to convert
various numeric and character representations of dates and times into R's
standard POSIXct (date-time) format. It simplifies the often-tricky process
of handling date/time data imported from other statistical software or
sources.
11 rk.doe NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.doe 0.0.1 FALSE
An RKWard plugin for generating Full Factorial, Fractional Factorial, and
Response Surface designs using 'DoE.base, FrF2.'. Design Generation: Create
Full Factorial, Fractional Factorial, and Response Surface designs and
specialized ANOVA and interaction plots for experimental designs.
12 rk.dplyr
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.dplyr/index.html
0.1.3 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.dplyr 0.1.3 TRUE An RKWard plugin for
data table combination and manipulation using the 'dplyr' library.
13 rk.flextable NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.flextable 0.0.2 FALSE
RKWard plugin that provides a graphical interface for the powerful
flextable package. It allows users to easily create, format, and export
professional tables for scientific publications and reports directly from
the RKWard GUI, without writing complex R code.
14 rk.forcats
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.forcats/index.html
0.1.7 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.forcats 0.1.7 TRUE An RKWard plugin
package for factor manipulation using the 'forcats' library.
15 rk.ggsurvey
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.ggsurvey/index.html
0.1.3 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.ggsurvey 0.1.7 FALSE A plugin package
analyze complex survey designs with custom plugins and the 'ggsurvey'
package.
17 rk.googlesheets4 NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.googlesheets4 0.0.1
FALSE
This package provides a suite of RKWard plugins that create a graphical
user interface for the popular `googlesheets4` R package. It is designed to
bridge the gap between desktop RKWard sessions and cloud-based Google
Sheets, allowing for authentication, reading, writing, and management of
sheets without needing to memorize API functions.
18 rk.gsub.sub
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.gsub.sub/index.html
0.0.7 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.gsub.sub 0.0.7 TRUE RKWard GUI for
sub() and gsub() to find and replace patterns in character vectors.
19 rk.gtsummary
https://mirror.fcix.net/kde-applicationdata/rkward/R/pckg/rk.gtsummary/index.html
0.1.0 https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.gtsummary 0.1.2 FALSE
An RKWard plugin to generate summary tables using the 'gtsummary' package,
supporting both standard data.frames (tbl_summary) and survey design
objects (tbl_svysummary).
20 rk.janitor NA NA https://github.com/AlfCano/rk.janitor 0.0.1 FALSE
This package provides a suite of RKWard plugins that create a graphical
user interface for the **[janitor](https://github.com/sfirke/janitor)** R

messages.subject: Mac Installation
messages.body_plain:
Am Fri, 23 Jan 2026 12:20:54 -0600
schrieb DES Alfonso Cano Robles <alfonsociologo at gmail.com>:

> *If there is anything I can do to help, let me know.*
> *Regards*
> *Alfonso*

thanks for offering! Whether you can help, depends on how far you want to dig
in. A rough outline of the steps involved:

1. To build rkward from sources on Mac, you'll need to setup "craft":
   https://community.kde.org/Get_Involved/development/Mac
   craft rkward && craft --package rkward
2. What I believe to be at the heart of the current problem is that we force
   QWebEngine to run inside the main process on Mac (rkward/main.cpp, the "#if
   defined(Q_OS_MACOS)"-section near line 140. Those lines would simply have to
   be removed.
3. However, that would currently break after packaging, and installing, due
   a bug in the craft packaging. This tries to convert absolute references to
   library locations to relative ones, essentially by a large number of calls
   to install_name_tools from a python script
   (craft/bin/Packager/MacOSBasPackager.py). This incorrectly makes references
   using "@executable_path/...", which breaks for the auxiliary qwebengine
   process (forgot, where exactly), as this is installed in a different
   directory. It should be adapted to use @loader_path, instead (see e.g.
   https://wincent.dev/wiki/%40executable_path%2C_%40load_path_and_%40rpath for
   some technical background).
4. Then that would need a solid round of testing, and finally a merge request
   to https://invent.kde.org/packaging/craft .

I can probably help with step 3, so if you can get as far as step 2, that's
helpful, already. We'd probably need a couple of rounds of trial-and-patch,
though.

Regards
Thomas
